stem:
A trolley on a smooth surface is attached by springs to fixed blocks as shown in Fig. 4.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The trolley oscillates horizontally about its equilibrium position with an amplitude of 12 cm. Fig. 4.2 shows the variation of the acceleration *a* of the trolley with displacement *x* from its equilibrium position. Friction between the trolley and the surface can be assumed to be negligible.

[[fig:f2]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the features of the line in Fig. 4.2 that demonstrate that the motion of the trolley is simple harmonic.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use Fig. 4.2 to determine the period *T* of the oscillations of the trolley.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: On the line of the graph of Fig. 4.2, label with the letter P one point where the kinetic energy of the trolley is zero.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: On the line of the graph of Fig. 4.2, label with the letter Q an approximate position of one point where the kinetic energy of the trolley is equal to the potential energy stored in the springs.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.1
figures.alt: A trolley on a smooth surface is connected by springs to fixed blocks on either side.

figures.caption: Fig. 4.2
figures.alt: A straight line with negative slope on a graph of acceleration a in m s⁻² against displacement x in cm, running from about (−12, 0.8) to (12, −0.8).
